recognize_zh: 視野中許多紅血球比中央小淋巴球的核還小、染色深且缺乏中央淡染區（central pallor），呈圓球狀，並夾雜略帶藍灰的多染性紅血球，符合遺傳性球形紅血球症的球形紅血球（spherocytes）。
features: Numerous small, round, densely staining red cells lacking central pallor (spherocytes)
Spherocytes are smaller than the nucleus of the adjacent small lymphocyte
Scattered larger bluish polychromatophilic red cells indicating reticulocytosis
Admixed normal discocytes with central pallor, producing a dimorphic appearance
Occasional crenated red cells, likely preparation artifact
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a mixed population of red cells with numerous spherocytes, which are small, round and hyperchromatic without central pallor and measure less than the diameter of the small lymphocyte nucleus in the center of the field. Scattered polychromatophilic cells are present. Some crenated cells are seen, likely artifactual. No schistocytes, agglutination or bite cells are identified. Findings are consistent with spherocytosis; in the appropriate clinical and family context (negative DAT, increased osmotic fragility or reduced EMA binding), this supports hereditary spherocytosis.

ddx.vs: Spherocytes look identical, so a positive direct antiglobulin test rather than morphology distinguishes immune hemolysis from hereditary spherocytosis.
MAHA shows schistocytes (helmet and triangular fragments) and thrombocytopenia, whereas this smear shows round intact spherocytes without fragments.
HPP shows marked microspherocytes together with bizarre fragments, budding forms and elliptocytes, which are not present here.
In thick areas all red cells lose central pallor uniformly, whereas true spherocytes coexist with normal discocytes in a thin, well-spread area as here.
